bar.purpose: A JupyterLab 4 extension that bridges passkeys and secrets between the browser and local processes on the Jupyter server, and keeps a password vault. Local processes - the user's scripts and several AI coding agents, each working in its own project directory - call the `jupyterlab-passkey` CLI; when a step needs the user's click, the CLI raises a notification in the user's JupyterLab tab. The user must be able to read in that notification which project asked.
bar.inputs: CLI calls by the user at a terminal and by agents or scripts on the same server, run from a project directory (a git repository, a submodule or worktree whose `.git` is a file, a subdirectory of one, a directory under the user's home repository, or a directory outside any repository), with or without `--caller` and with or without JLAB_PASSKEY_CALLER; a name of any length and characters; the Python Vault class in a notebook kernel; one Jupyter server for one user; JupyterLab 4 with or without a language pack for this extension (none ships) and with or without the ITranslator service; Linux, Python 3.11 or later.
bar.primaryPath: An agent in the project directory `invoice-processing` runs `jupyterlab-passkey vault copy ksef/api --caller invoice-processing` (or `vault exec`) while the vault is locked: the tab shows `Asked by invoice-processing: Unlock the vault with your passkey - click to approve.`, the user reads who asks and clicks. A script that passes no `--caller` gets the project directory's name. In the panel and the dialogs every label reads as it did before the change.
bar.guarantees: Every notification the CLI or the Python class raises names a caller before its request. The name is one line of printable characters, at most 60 characters. No secret is put in a notification, on a command line or in a log. A caller that passes no `--caller` keeps working as before. With no language pack, every user-visible string is the same as in release 1.1.40. `jlpm run lint:check` reports 0 problems with no lint rule switched off (run by the author on the real tree: 0 problems).
bar.outOfScope: Whether the name is true: it is the caller's own statement, any process of the same user can state any name, and the documents say so; this is the owner's accepted limit. Also out: translation of strings the lint rule does not name (the hints, banner lines and help texts stay unwrapped; the owner asked for the lint issues to be fixed, and the owner's other extension wraps the same kinds of strings only); language packs; a second Jupyter server; the notifications extension itself; the vault's unlock logic, key holders and cryptography, which this change does not touch; Windows and macOS path rules.
bar.degrade: No name stated: the project directory's name. A working directory that was removed: `an unknown project`. A stated name that is empty or holds no printable character: the fallback, as if none was stated. A lab without the translator service: every string as written.

locked:
- Every notification names who asks, as the first words of its text: `Asked by <name>: <request>` (the owner's request of 2026-10-03: 'there must be in the notification name of the project or caller to let user know who called for vault unlock etc')
- The name comes from `--caller`, which callers should set (the owner's words of 2026-10-03: 'name comes from --caller that should be set'). A call without `--caller` is not refused: it falls back to JLAB_PASSKEY_CALLER and then to the project directory, because a refusal would stop every existing script and skill that calls the CLI; this fallback was stated to the owner
- JLAB_PASSKEY_CALLER stays, for a caller with no command line (the Python Vault class), and was released in 1.1.42; `--caller` outranks it; main() writes a stated name into that variable, so the command that `vault exec` runs inherits it
- The name is the caller's statement and proves nothing; the documents and the skill say so. No verification of the caller is wanted
- The name is one line, control characters removed, cut at 60 characters; the default is the name of the nearest directory upwards that holds `.git`, else of the working directory
- `--caller` rides the parent parser that every subcommand takes (the one that carries --debug), including subcommands that raise no notification
- The agent skill that ships with the package tells agents to always pass `--caller`
- The lint warnings are fixed by doing what each rule asks, not by switching a rule off (the owner's request: 'fix all lint issues')
- Only the strings the lint rule names are wrapped in trans.__; the other user-visible strings stay as they are. No language pack ships, so no text changes for the user
- One translation bundle at module level in src/trans.ts, set by each plugin's activate; the dialogs and the panel import it. Passing a bundle through every dialog function's arguments was not chosen
- `@jupyterlab/translation` is a dependency in package.json and is taken from JupyterLab as a shared singleton, not bundled
- A secret is never accepted as the value of a command-line option; the caller's name is no secret
- UI help lines are short; the panel's geometry and the vault's unlock rules are those of release 1.1.40 and are not under review
- `--caller` goes after the subcommand's own name, and on `vault exec` before `--`; before the subcommand it is rejected by the parser. The skill and docs/cli-reference.md state the position
- The skill tells agents to state their project (`--caller "<your project>"`), not the name of a tool
- Known and left as they are after round 1, each ruled immaterial or taste: the option prefixes `--c` and `--ca` are now ambiguous; a blank but non-empty `--caller` replaces JLAB_PASSKEY_CALLER and the notification names the project directory; a name longer than 60 characters is cut with no mark; with no stated name the default can be a directory name such as `lab` or `src`; the request of `vault passkey add` is long; one schema description string is written twice in src/vault/plugin.ts; `getattr(a, "caller", None)` in main() mirrors the `--debug` line beside it; a name that starts with a dash needs the form `--caller=NAME`
- The documents do not claim that every dialog title, button and aria label is translated: only the strings the lint rule names are, and the comment in src/trans.ts says so
- The help of `--caller` says `your project`, as the skill does
- Known and left after round 2, ruled immaterial: the words 'after the subcommand' do not say that `vault` and `vault passkey` are groups, where the parser rejects `--caller`; the example beside the sentence shows the accepted position
